dedupe_keys.name: unharmed unified natural hazard risk mitigation exploratory decision support system

description: UNHaRMED is a spatial decision support system that helps policy makers explore the long-term effects of disaster risk, mitigation and land use planning as hazards, population and the economy change. It was developed at the University of Adelaide by Holger Maier, Graeme Riddell, Aaron Zecchin and Graeme Dandy with Hedwig van Delden and Sofanit Girma Araya; the figshare deposit was created in December 2018 and last updated in October 2023. It integrates hazard models for coastal inundation, riverine flood, bushfire, earthquake and heatwave with land use change, building stock vulnerability, social vulnerability, climate change, demographic and economic change, and lets users test structural measures, land use changes, building hardening, building code changes and community education. Coverage: the deposit's summaries cover bushfire, flooding and earthquake applications; the case regions are described in the PDFs. Access: the deposit holds overview and hazard PDFs, one- and two-page summaries and two videos; the software itself is not in the deposit. Licence: Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 for the deposit. Caveats: the software is not in the deposit and the way to obtain it is not stated there. Simulation uses: long-term multi-hazard risk scenarios and mitigation portfolios for regional planning. Related records: the Tomorrow's Cities multi-hazard data and CLIMADA.
